question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

events.title: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
events.description:

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping maintains firm control over the Chinese Communist Party and state institutions as of mid-2026, with analysts widely expecting him to secure a fourth term at the 21st National Congress scheduled for late 2027. Recent developments, including ongoing anti-corruption purges in the military and civilian ranks, the July Beidaihe leadership conclave, and appointments of loyalists to key posts, reinforce elite cohesion and deter challenges. No designated successor has emerged, and Xi has shown no public signals of stepping aside before the congress. Trader consensus on the low probability of removal before 2027 reflects the absence of visible succession mechanisms, health disclosures, or factional opposition in this compressed timeframe. Unlikely but plausible shifts could still arise from a sudden medical event, major external crisis mismanagement, or undetected elite fractures, though primary sources indicate sustained consolidation rather than instability.
